subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in temp artifact provenance model, and if so should it be limited to runtime/install/doctor safety or also expose an agent/tool artifact classification API?
rationale: The request is aligned with safe defaults, but the durable state model, cleanup semantics, and core-vs-plugin/API boundary are product and storage-architecture choices that should not be inferred by automation.

options.title: Core runtime safety only
options.body: Implement doctor/runtime checks for temp-backed critical paths and leave workflow-specific artifact classification to plugins or skills until a core API gap is proven.

options.title: Core SQLite artifact provenance
options.body: Design a first-class SQLite-backed artifact provenance API for agent/tool-created temp outputs, including cleanup classes and janitor semantics.

options.title: Plugin or ClawHub package first
options.body: Keep core unchanged for now and ask the reporter to publish the skill-audit/janitor workflow externally while maintainers watch for repeated demand.

recommendation.title: Core runtime safety only
recommendation.body: Implement doctor/runtime checks for temp-backed critical paths and leave workflow-specific artifact classification to plugins or skills until a core API gap is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current blame and history signal across the temp helper, static temp guardrail, and repository-scoping comments involved in this decision.
